propositions: Long-running LLM gate operations emit no output to stdout/stderr between start and final verdict, causing supervisor stall watchdogs (600s default) to kill healthy runs before completion.
Gate operations routinely run for minutes (27-150s observed) with multiple phases producing no instrumentation at default log level (WARNING) or even at DEBUG level.
The phase logs that exist fire only after phase completion at INFO level, and the shared LLM seam uses non-streaming synchronous calls with no incremental output.
An autonomous agent orchestrating rebar was killed mid-epic-close by a harness stall watchdog, leaving work stranded in_progress despite all code changes having landed.
Silence during gate operations is deliberate per ADR 0089 and documented as acceptable (no total-runtime timer exists), making this a feature-request rather than a regression.

Supervisor budgets and gate operation wall-clock ranges are undocumented or deliberately unspecified, preventing operators from raising budgets deliberately or distinguishing healthy long runs from hung processes.
